evidence: src/presentation/handlers/PayrollController.ts: constructor(private readonly payroll: PayrollService, private readonly audit: PayrollAuditService) injects business-layer services, which presentation may depend on
submit(actor, payload: HoursPayload) passes the work to this.payroll.submitHours and this.audit.log and returns { id: sheet.id }, with no business logic in the controller
approve(actor, timesheetId) passes the work to this.payroll.approve and returns { approved: sheet.approved }, reading a flag the business layer computed
export(week) maps the results of this.payroll.run(week) through the presentation view payslipRow, which is presentation formatting
parsedVerdict.reasoning: PayrollController is a presentation-layer controller, and everything in it fits that role. It declares a transport payload shape (HoursPayload). Its constructor injects two business-layer services, which is the layer presentation may depend on, so this is dependency wiring. Its methods unpack the input, pass work to PayrollService and PayrollAuditService, and turn the results into response shapes or view rows through payslipView. The file holds no domain invariant, calculation or decision. Hours submission, approval and the payroll run are all delegated to business services. The audit calls go to a business-layer service and do not decide anything themselves. The file uses no framework types or decorators that belong to another layer, and the deterministic checks raised no candidate flags.
